body: Agreed, we would like to continue using Godot and hope that this compatibility can be added so we can build android apps using C#.

Thanks for reaching out! It seems there are a few misunderstandings.

First of all, Microsoft is not deprecating **all** MonoVM runtime packages, only the packages for desktop platforms (Windows, Linux, macOS). You can see the full list of the packages that were deprecated in the [link you posted](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/compatibility/deployment/9.0/monovm-packages).

Like the Microsoft announcement says, the desktop MonoVM runtime packages are not the default configuration for .NET publish scenarios. You would've only been using the MonoVM runtime on these platforms if you enabled an undocumented SDK switch. This is also the case for Godot on these platforms. The default runtime, CoreCLR, tends to perform better on these platforms so there's no reason to use MonoVM.

To reiterate, this breaking change does not impact MonoVM's support for its primary shipping scenario: iOS, Android, WASM, etc. [^1]

Second, `linux-bionic` is not the default nor the recommended runtime for exporting to Android using Godot. This was added in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/97908 as an advanced option for users to export using NativeAOT. There is no real support for NativeAOT on Android yet[^2], so the only way to get it is using the `linux-bionic` runtime, and some advanced users wanted to do that.

However, I must reiterate that this is not the recommended runtime. It's not enabled by default, and you shouldn't use it if you don't know what you are doing. The `linux-bionic` runtime has a number of limitations and is most likely not what you want to use. If you enable it, be aware that there are a lot of things that may not work and it's only intended to be used for NativeAOT, not MonoVM.

I hope that clears all the misunderstandings. In short, Godot is unaffected by these deprecations.

[^1]: https://github.com/dotnet/docs/issues/41366#issuecomment-2210713569
[^2]: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/106748

> I see, thanks for your answer, so the problem were actually using NativeAOT, which isn't supported without the linux-bionic. Is there any other way to use NativeAOT without it?

No, for Android `linux-bionic` is the only way to use NativeAOT at the moment. Be aware of its limitations.

I'll reiterate that MonoVM has nothing to do with NativeAOT, so if you are seeing errors regarding MonoVM then your project is likely not configured to use NativeAOT properly. You'll have to share your `.csproj` if you want us to be able to provide more help, but the most likely scenario is you forgot `<PublishAot>true</PublishAot>` or it's under a condition that doesn't match.

> Or is it planned at anytime to have such option?

When NativeAOT is supported on Android upstream, it will likely work on Godot too. See issue upstream:

- https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/106748

> Also, even disabling both the NativeAOT and linux-bionic options, when running on android, it seems to throw SSL errors when trying to hit HTTPS endpoints, is there any workaround on it?

You'll have to provide more details about this. What is the endpoint? Does it work on a C# console application? Does it work on a web browser (i.e.: Google Chrome)?

But it's most likely not an issue on Godot's side, since you are getting a proper exception and not a crash. It may be a bug on your code or upstream on the .NET runtime.

Looks like you are targeting .NET 10 which is still in preview, using .NET 9 your MRP works fine for me. Since .NET 10 is still in preview, there may still be bugs. As mentioned earlier, it's most likely not an issue on Godot's side. It looks like it may be a bug upstream on .NET.
